fix.title: Fix what Dispatch heard
fix.everyTimeUnavailable: Type what you meant to add it to your Fix-It List too.

fix.everyTimeHelpTitle: When to fix it every time
fix.everyTimeHelp: Tick this for a word Dispatch gets wrong the same way again and again, like "quad code" for "Claude Code". It adds a rule to your Fix-It List that changes it in every dictation from now on. Leave it off for one-off mistakes, and for real words you might also say, like "spanner".

smartSpacing.label: Smart Spacing
smartSpacing.description: Add a space before dictated text when the cursor is right after a word, so back-to-back dictations don't run together. Works in apps that report their text to Windows accessibility.

cleanUpDictation.label: Clean Up Dictation
cleanUpDictation.description: Run every dictation through the cleanup model before pasting. Turn off to paste exactly what you said.

cleanupSetup.noOllama: Cleanup removes filler words and fixes punctuation with a small AI model that runs on your computer, through Ollama. It's off until Ollama is set up, so your dictations paste exactly as you said them.
cleanupSetup.noModel: Ollama is running, but the cleanup model ({{model}}) isn't downloaded yet. Cleanup is off until it is, so your dictations paste exactly as you said them.

cleanupSetup.autoCheck: Dispatch also checks each time it starts.
cleanupSetup.stillMissing: Still not found. Make sure Ollama is running, then check again.
cleanupSetup.ready: Ollama found. AI cleanup is on.

handy.title: Handy
handy.description: The open source app Dispatch is built on, created by CJ Pais
handy.details: Dispatch started as a fork of Handy, the free and open source speech-to-text app created by CJ Pais. Handy does the hard parts: the global shortcuts, recording, fast local transcription with models like Whisper and Parakeet, and pasting the text into whatever app you're using. Dispatch adds AI cleanup and a few personal touches on top. Handy is released under the MIT license. Thank you, CJ, for building it and sharing it with everyone.

setting.title: Keep Recordings
setting.description: Every recording can be replayed in History and used later to train Dispatch on your voice. Transcripts are always kept, and starred dictations keep their audio.

confirm.title_one: Move {{count}} old recording to the Recycle Bin?
confirm.title_other: Move {{count}} old recordings to the Recycle Bin?
confirm.body_one: Dispatch will keep your {{kept}} newest recordings and move the other one ({{length}}, {{size}}) to the Recycle Bin. Its transcript stays in History.
confirm.body_other: Dispatch will keep your {{kept}} newest recordings and move the other {{count}} ({{length}}, {{size}}) to the Recycle Bin. Their transcripts stay in History, and starred dictations keep their audio.
confirm.note: You can restore them from the Recycle Bin. Recordings that aren't kept can't be replayed here or used to train Dispatch on your voice.

question.title: Keep your recordings?
question.body: Dispatch keeps the audio of every dictation, so you can replay any of them here and, later, train Dispatch on your voice. That's about 2 MB per minute of talking. Transcripts are kept either way.
question.later: You can change this any time in Settings, Advanced.
